name: libxsmm-full512-padded-272-byte-a-slices
hypothesis: Implement the selected padding experiment in the full512 kernel: allocate 139264 bytes, pack 512 slices at 272-byte intervals, and update both packed-A consumer strides and rewinds. Each slice contains 256 data bytes followed by 16 unused bytes. The second row half still starts at byte 128; the final data byte is at offset 139247, within the allocation. B and C addressing, FP32 FMOPA order, one kernel call, SME transitions, general-size fallback, and both complete license notices remain unchanged. This corrected layout is absent from the supplied measured history. The hypothesis is that padding changes scratch cache mapping; cache geometry and benefit are unverified. No tools or tests were run. Compilation, full-GEMM correctness, and performance require fresh validation under the fixed gates and repeated paired controls with battery power and settings unchanged. No gain or throughput above 1800 GFLOP/s is established.
